who: Cheikh Anta Mbacké Babou, historian of Islam and West Africa at Pennsylvania since 2002; PhD Michigan State 2002.

evidence.says: Penn lists Cheikh Babou / Cheikh Anta Babou as a history professor, joining in 2002, with a Michigan State PhD in 2002.
Authority gives Cheikh Babou as a name variant and identifies the University of Pennsylvania historian and author of Fighting the Greater Jihad.
Other candidate studied German studies and completed a Bayreuth dissertation in 2016; the authority identifies a modern German literature teacher at UCAD, Dakar.

notes: Penn affiliation, field and exact doctorate match. The other Babou authority identifies a different scholar.

who: Historian of modern Korea at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa; PhD Columbia 2010.

Heroes and Toilers source note identifies Cheehyung Harrison Kim as assistant professor of history at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

notes: Exact name, university, book and doctoral institution agree; authority places him at Mānoa by 2018, before the listed students.

who: Historian of South Asia at UCLA since 1993; PhD Chicago, South Asian Languages and Civilizations, 1992.

notes: Same UCLA historian throughout the students’ period; Chicago doctorate agrees with the AHA record.

who: David M. Goodblatt, historian of ancient Jewish history at UC San Diego, 1988–2017; PhD Brown 1972.

evidence.says: UCSD identifies David Goodblatt as teaching there since 1988, PhD Brown 1972, working on ancient Jewish history; lists Rabbinic Instruction in Sasanian Babylonia.
Authority’s UC San Diego notice identifies David Mordecai Goodblatt, history professor, Brown Religious Studies PhD 1972, and UCSD appointment from 1988 to 2017.

notes: Authority and department identify the same historian; UCSD employment covers all three students’ years. AHA supplies no own doctorate to compare.

who: William Henry Covici Propp, UC San Diego historian of the ancient Near East and Hebrew Bible; PhD Harvard 1985.

evidence.says: UCSD’s William Propp page gives the full name William Henry Covici Propp, ancient Near Eastern and biblical studies, and works including Water in the Wilderness and Exodus 19–40.
Authority explicitly links William Propp and William Henry Covici Propp to the UCSD faculty page; its Exodus 19–40 source identifies him as UCSD professor of history and Judaic studies.
UCSD lists William H. C. Propp in History, Biblical Studies and Semitic Languages, with a Harvard PhD in 1985.

notes: Full name, institution, field, works and Harvard doctorate identify n86129215. The W. Alan Propp candidate has no supporting link to this supervisor.

who: Bill (William) Winders, sociologist in Georgia Tech’s School of History and Sociology; PhD sociology, Emory 2001.

evidence.says: Georgia Tech lists Bill Winders as professor in History and Sociology, Emory sociology PhD 2001, and author of The Politics of Food Supply.

Authority links William Winders with the variant Bill Winders and The Politics of Food Supply; its Grains (2017) note identifies him as associate professor in Georgia Tech’s School of History and Sociology.

notes: William/Bill variants are explicit in LC. Institution during the students’ period, works and Emory doctorate agree.

who: Historian of science at UBC; PhD history of science, Institute for History of Science and Technology, Moscow, 1989.

evidence.says: UBC history faculty page lists doctoral supervision of Ken Corbett (2020), Eric Michael Johnson (2019) and Somaditya Banerjee (2013), with the corresponding dissertation titles.
Institutional CV identifies UBC history professor Alexei B. Kojevnikov and a 1989 history-of-science PhD from the Institute for History of Science and Technology, USSR Academy of Sciences, Moscow.
Authority cites his UBC faculty page and identifies the same 1989 Moscow doctorate; The Copenhagen Network source places him in UBC’s History Department.

notes: All three listed students are named on his UBC supervision list; the authority and doctorate match.
